title: Zero-inflated Poisson regression for counts with structural zeros
summary: A logistic model for being a structural zero and a Poisson model for the count among those at risk, with the count part's rate ratio.

sizing._why: No zero-inflated form is in the catalog; sizing needs both the structural-zero probability and the count distribution and is a simulation.

pinned_defaults: R: zeroinfl(visits ~ treated | 1). Without the bar, pscl uses the SAME covariates in the zero-inflation model as in the count model.
Python: exog_infl given explicitly (intercept only). statsmodels' default is intercept-only, the opposite of pscl's.

Python: standard errors from the numerical Hessian of the model's own log-likelihood. In statsmodels 0.14.2, ZeroInflatedPoisson's bse come from an analytic Hessian that disagrees with the log-likelihood's curvature: 0.0752 against 0.0761 for the rate ratio here, 0.0956 against 0.1060 for the inflation term. R's pscl agrees with the curvature.
_interpretation: The count part's rate ratio applies AMONG THOSE AT RISK, not to the whole population. A zero-inflated model needs a mechanism for structural zeros; many zeros alone are often fitted as well by a negative binomial (negative-binomial-rate-ratio).
